message.content: The uploader hammers storage after a network drop and we get 503s for minutes. What should a failed part do?

content.thinking: Every client retrying together is the thundering herd.

content.text: I recommend **capped exponential backoff with full jitter**. The wait doubles from one second and stops growing at thirty, and each client sleeps a random time up to that wait. A fixed interval is the thing to avoid: every client that lost its connection at the same moment comes back at the same moment, and storage sheds them all again.

message.content: Agreed, build that in src/upload/backoff.rs and run the upload tests.

content.text: I wrote the wait as a pure function of the attempt number and a random source, so a test can pin it.

content.text: One red: `parks_after_the_attempt_limit`. The counter in `src/upload/queue.rs` compared with `>=` after incrementing, so a part stopped one try early. I changed it to `>` and the limit is five attempts, after which the part sits in the local queue and shows as paused.

message.content: Good. Should paused parts retry on their own when the network returns?

content.text: Yes. The reachability watcher unparks everything on reconnect and each part starts over at attempt one, since the failures that parked it say nothing about the new connection.
